status: PROPOSAL pending the owner's review: the queries, floors, thresholds and weights are editorial choices. Change them here; the code reads them on every run.

derivedMetricsAmendment.why: The outlier ratio, the engagement score and the ranking are metrics derived from YouTube API Data. YouTube's Developer Policies (III.E.4) forbid derived metrics unless the API project has accepted the 'Additional policies for derived metrics and data storage' amendment through the YouTube API Services Audit and Quota Extension Form (Section 5 -> 'Analytics & Reporting'). Set accepted to true, with the date and YouTube's reference, only after YouTube confirms it for the project this key belongs to. Until then live runs stop before the first API call; --fixtures runs (synthetic data) are unaffected.

compliance.retentionWhy: Developer Policies III.E.4: API Data fetched with an API key may be kept no longer than 30 calendar days. Every run deletes cache entries and out/topics reports older than this; the value can be lowered, never raised.

window.note: search.list publishedAfter = the run date's UTC midnight minus this many days (a whole-day boundary keeps the search cache stable for a day).

search.note: order=viewCount per the brief. Google warns that a non-relevance order combined with publishedAfter 'might result in a smaller or incomplete result set'; --orders viewCount,relevance widens the net at one extra search call per query.

format.note: A Short is at most 3 minutes and vertical or square. player.embedWidth/embedHeight give the aspect ratio when YouTube knows it; without it only videos of 60 s or less count as Shorts.

floors.note: minViews: a candidate needs at least this many views (Shorts count every start, so their floor is higher). baselineFloor: the median is never taken below this, so a 40-view channel cannot produce a 300x 'outlier'. minOutlier: the ratio a video needs to be listed.

baseline.note: The channel median uses its most recent uploads (one page of 50 by default), excluding the candidate itself, uploads younger than minAgeDays (still ramping), older than maxAgeDays, and live or upcoming broadcasts. It compares Shorts with Shorts and long-form with long-form, and prefers uploads published under the same view-counting rules as the candidate.

scoring.note: rank = 100 x (weights . components) x confidence. Components are 0-1: outlier = log2(ratio)/log2(saturation); recency halves every recencyHalfLifeDays; engagement compares (likes + comments) per view with this run's median for the same format (0.5 when hidden); fit comes from taxonomy.json. These are the topic finder's own metrics, not YouTube data.
